info.description:
The Zooza API gives your integration access to a Zooza company's programmes, classes, sessions,
registrations, attendance and invoices.

## Regions

Each region has its own host (see the server list). A key works only in the region of the company
that created it.

## Authentication

Exchange your key's `client_id` and `client_secret`, together with the email of an owner of the
company, for an access token at `POST /v3/token`. Send the token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
Tokens last 60 minutes and there is no refresh token: request a new one when it expires.

## Company

A key acts for the company that created it, and only for that company.

## Access groups

Each operation names the access groups that may call it and its cost in points (`x-zooza-access`, also
shown at the end of its description). A key holds one or more groups and may call the operations of all of
them. `GET /v3/me` lists everything your key may call.

## Rate limits

Every operation costs points from your company's budget per minute and per day, which all its keys share.
The budget comes from the company's rate tier (`x-zooza-tiers`). The `X-RateLimit-*` headers report it
**in points, not in requests**. Over budget, the API
answers `429` with `Retry-After`. `GET /v3/me` costs nothing and shows what is left.

## Dates and times

Dates and times are in the local time of your region, without an offset: EU `Europe/Bratislava`, UK
`Europe/London`, ASIA `Asia/Dubai`. Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`, date-times `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.

## Amounts

Whether prices include VAT depends on the company's VAT setting. By default prices include VAT, and
VAT is calculated out of them. A company can instead enter prices without VAT, and VAT is then added
on top.

## Lists and pagination

Most lists share one envelope: `{total, page, page_size, settings, data}`, where `page` is zero-based,
`page_size` is the number per page and `data` holds the items (`GET /v3/events`, `/schedules`,
`/customer_invoices`, `/places`, `/users`). Three lists differ:

- `GET /v3/courses` returns a plain array of every programme, without pagination.
- `GET /v3/registrations` returns `{total, total_capped, page, offset, results}`: the items are in
  `results`, and `total` stops counting at 500 (`total_capped` says when).
- `GET /v3/calendar` returns `{settings, info, data}` for one date range, without pagination;
  `GET /v3/attendance` returns a plain array.

## Errors

- `401`, `403`, `422`, `429`, `503` and `504` use the `Error` body: `error`, `message`, `request_id`
  and, on `422`, `errors` with every problem found (up to 100).
- `400` uses the `RequestError` envelope: `errors` and `request_valid`, with messages in the company's
  language. Each entry maps a four-digit error code to its message. Branch on the code, not the message:
  codes never change meaning, messages are reworded and translated. Every code, with its English
  message, is listed in the error code reference (`x-zooza-error-codes` in this document).
- Any operation can also answer `404` with the `Error` body (no such path), or `500` with either body.
- `POST /v3/token` answers with OAuth error bodies (`error`, `error_description`).

## Field naming

Fields that start with `__` are copied from a related record or calculated by Zooza, so lists can be read
without extra requests. They are read-only: to change one, change the record it comes from.

| Pattern | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `__{record}__{field}` | `{field}` of a related record | `__courses__price` on a class is the price of its programme |
| `__calc__{name}` | A value Zooza calculates | `__calc__debt` on a registration is the total it has been charged |
| `__view__{name}` | A value shaped for display | |

Fields without the prefix belong to the record itself.
